Hi Nora — thanks for the precise questions. Answers below (I tried to keep each item short so you can paste into your risk note):

1) "Model outputs" definition:
- Textual generation returned to the caller (the raw string or structured JSON the model emits) — always considered an "output."
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, dense vectors, reranker scores) are treated as separate artifact types in our retention model; they do not automatically inherit the same TTL as textual outputs but are configurable.

2) Sandbox vs production TTLs (examples):
- Sandbox (default): 
  • Debug logs (request/response metadata, transient traces): retained 7 days (for troubleshooting) then purged.
  • Persisted outputs (if you enable "persist sandbox outputs" for debugging): retained 30 days by default; you can opt to set to 0 (no persistence).
- Hosted production (default): 
  • Debug logs: retained 30 days for platform health/observability; can be shortened with enterprise contract.
  • Persisted outputs: 90 days by default for analytics; can be configured to 0 for customers on Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated / Private: 
  • Retention is fully configurable by the customer (including 0 days). On Private, data never leaves your VPC and we provide KMS/HSM integration.

3) Debug traces and KV caches: 
- Short-lived traces and partial KV cache snapshots used for live debugging are stored in the region handling the request (for your POC we'll use us-east-1). These traces are encrypted and accessible only to SRE/Platform on a need basis; access is logged. Default TTL for such traces is 7 days (sandbox) or 30 days (hosted prod).

4) Residency: 
- For the POC we will keep sandbox artifacts in us-east-1. For production you can choose EU (eu-west-1) or APAC regions. Dedicated can be provisioned in your required region.

5) Encryption & access control: 
- At-rest encryption by default with Redwood-managed KMS; customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private.
- RBAC for access to stored outputs and logs; audit logs available via the console and exported to your SIEM.

6) Opt-out/controls: 
- For hosted API you can: set retention=0, disable persisted outputs, and enable strict request-only processing.
- For Dedicated/Private we will provision configuration that enforces retention=0 if required by your compliance team.

Attachments and links: I've attached our short retention options PDF and the privacy matrix. Also linking the short POC configuration doc for the deep-dive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_privacy-matrix

If you want a single-config example to paste into your internal template, here's one you can copy: 

Example: ChloeTech sandbox (recommended POC)
- region: us-east-1
- debug_traces_ttl_days: 7
- persisted_outputs_enabled: true
- persisted_outputs_ttl_days: 30
- embeddings_retention_days: 30 (configurable)
- encryption: redwood-managed-kms (option to supply CMK on Dedicated)

I'll also upload a one-click JSON snippet to the HubSpot deal so your infra folks can import.
